subject: Re: Acero Health private deployment — guardrails, data responsibilities, and open questions
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-18T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment guardrails + items we promised to capture

Thanks again for the time this morning, Sanjay — good conversation. Quick recap and the open items we said we'd pull together for your Security & Architecture team.

Key points from the call:
- Acero will evaluate a Redwood Private (VPC) deployment on GCP in us-west1.
- High-level data classification: PHI/PII in payloads (patient name, MRN), provider metadata, and a small set of logs/access events.
- Primary constraints: (1) no persistent PHI leaving the VPC, (2) audit-grade access logs for model input/output, (3) ability to define 30/90/365 day retention windows per dataset.

What we promised to deliver:
1) A draft data flow diagram showing network boundaries and where PII may touch Redwood components — attached (acero-dataflow-draft.pdf).
2) A short question matrix on retention, KMS, and logging (attached spreadsheet).
3) Proposed next-step: 30-minute deep-dive with your infra/security to walk the diagram and capture any air-gap or egress exceptions.

Open clarifying questions for your team (please forward to LegalOps / Infra as needed):
- For any input data that includes PHI, do you require that we never persist any model-generated outputs to object storage by default? Or is ephemeral disk + audit log acceptable?
- Do you have a minimum encryption-at-rest requirement (Customer-managed KMS) for any token caches or KV caches used for inference?
- Any preferred sysadmin ops model (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed bastion) for certificate/key rotation?

Next steps I propose:
- Sanjay: share the names for the 2 people from LegalOps and one infra lead to include on the deep-dive.
- Connor: I asked you to prepare a one-slide summary of our private egress controls and the fallback policy for capacity-constrained requests.

Thanks — I'll schedule the deep-dive once Sanjay confirms attendees.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0138
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acerohealth.com>

Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acerohealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment guardrails + items we promised to capture

Hi Vivek — thanks for this. Attaching internally. Quick answers inline:  

- Persisting outputs: Legal prefers that any model outputs containing PHI not be persisted to long-term object stores by default. Ephemeral in-memory or ephemeral disk during the request lifecycle is OK as long as we get immutable audit logs that show the request-id, timestamp, and user-id.
- KMS: yes — we require CMEK for any disk or storage holding token/kv caches.
- Ops model: we prefer customer-managed bastion and key rotation; Redwood can document the automation steps and we can schedule a runbook review.

I cc'd LegalOps to confirm retention windows and any compliance language. LegalOps: can you confirm whether a 90-day default retention for non-PHI telemetry + 30/365 options for other categories works? Also flag any specific contractual language you will need re: egress guarantees and air-gapped options.

I'll introduce infra contacts once LegalOps confirms retention.

-Sanjay
From: LegalOps <legalops@acerohealth.com>

Date: 2027-03-18T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment guardrails + items we promised to capture

Vivek — thanks for the attachments. Two immediate asks from the legal/compliance team:  

1) Please provide a short paragraph describing where audit logs are stored, retention options, and whether logs contain full PII or redacted identifiers. We need this to route a SOC-2 scoping question.
2) Confirm whether Redwood supports an on-prem air-gapped option (full offline model serving) or whether the Private deployment will always require at least controlled egress for model updates/telemetry. If the latter, detail what telemetry is required and whether it can be routed via a customer proxy.

We have an internal window this Thursday for initial contract redlines — if we can provide the two items above by EOD Wednesday that would be very helpful.

- LegalOps (Acero Health)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: LegalOps <legalops@acerohealth.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acerohealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-18T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment guardrails + items we promised to capture

Hi LegalOps / Sanjay — Rachel from Product Security here. Answers below (high level; happy to expand in the deep-dive or provide a short attestation document).

1) Audit logs
- Storage: Audit logs (request metadata, request-id, user-id, timestamps, routing decisions) are written to customer-controlled Cloud Storage buckets in your VPC.
- PII in logs: By default we redact free-text model outputs from logs. Logs contain identifiers (user-id, request-id) and hashes for content fingerprints. Customer can opt-in to include full payloads for a specific project with explicit contractual acceptance.
- Retention: Flexible, configurable per ingestion stream. We can set TTLs at 30 / 90 / 365 days. Longer term archiving requires explicit consent and storage provisioning in your project.

2) Air-gap / on-prem options
- Fully air-gapped (no external egress, manual model updates via signed artifacts) is supported as an enterprise option but requires an on-prem bundle and a provisioning window; it is treated as a separate engagement.
- Redwood Private (VPC-hosted) will require occasional connectivity for model updates, security patching, and optional telemetry. Telemetry minimal set: health pings (no payloads), aggregated usage metrics, and crash reports. All telemetry can be routed through a customer-managed proxy and encrypted using CMEK.

3) KMS / KV caches
- We support customer-managed KMS for disk encryption and for wrapping model keys. Token/KV caches can be configured to use ephemeral memory only, or persisted with CMEK to customer GCS buckets in your project.

Attachments: I pushed a short checklist into the spreadsheet column (redwood-private-questions.xlsx) and updated the dataflow PDF legend to flag where PII could appear.

Proposed next step: let's lock a 30-min walkthrough on Thursday at 10:00am PT to walk the diagram and confirm retention SLOs. Vivek: can you schedule? Connor: can you bring the fallback/egress slide.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Product Security | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment guardrails + items we promised to capture

Thanks everyone — scheduling invite sent for Thu 2027-03-20 10:00am PT (30 min). Agenda: 1) review attached diagram + legend (5m), 2) retention & KMS defaults (10m), 3) egress / air-gap requirements and proxy options (10m), 4) next steps and contract redline owners (5m).

Quick summary of agreed positions so LegalOps has a note for redlines:
- Default: no model-generated PHI persisted to long-term object storage unless customer explicitly enables it.
- Audit logs: stored in customer-controlled buckets; redaction by default; retention configurable to 30/90/365.
- KMS: customer-managed CMEK supported and required for any persisted caches.
- Air-gap: fully air-gapped on-prem option available as separate delivery; Private (VPC) will need controlled egress for updates unless air-gap engagement purchased.

I'll bring the meeting notes and add owners for the contract items afterward. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
